hypothesis: When release(employee) and revokeGrant(employee) execute atomically in the same block (via Safe MultiSend) with release first, the GrantRevoked event must satisfy the conservation invariant: released + claimable + canceled = total
sub_hypothesis: With release first: released = vested_at_T > 0, claimable = 0 (vested == released), canceled = total - vested_at_T
adversarial_question: Does revokeGrant correctly observe the updated g.released written by the preceding release() sub-call within the same transaction?

timing_proof.note: Active vesting window guaranteed at time of MultiSend execution

execution_mechanism: Safe MultiSend batch — both sub-calls execute within the same Ethereum tx, same block, same block.timestamp (T)

invariants.ordering_effect: release() runs first: g.released is written to vested_at_T before revokeGrant() reads it
invariants.claimable_prediction: claimable = 0 because vested_at_T == released_at_revokedAt (release already captured all vested tokens)

assumptions.A2: EVM storage writes in a preceding sub-call are visible to subsequent sub-calls within the same transaction. This test observes behavior consistent with A2 but cannot independently prove A2, which is an EVM axiom. A2 violation would be observationally indistinguishable from a contract bug reading stale storage.

required_proofs: createGrant tx confirmed: grant.exists == true, params match
MultiSend tx confirmed: both sub-calls succeeded in same block
GrantRevoked.released == GrantRevoked.vested (release ran first, captured all vested)

safe_transactions_required.note: Verify beneficiary — release() checks isVerified(), will revert if not verified
CRITICAL: release must be first sub-call. Use Safe Transaction Builder to batch these two calls.
